Title: No-source refusal behavior
What this is: When the ask box has no sourced answer, it says so instead of writing one. Nothing a reader is told is ever generated to fill a gap.
Detail: When there is no sourced answer, say so. Never let the model fill the gap. Applies to every question path.
Session record: Build as a constraint on A01, in the same PR. Do not ship a natural-language entry point without it. || 2026-08-17 (g11). VERIFIED WORKING, ROW STAYS OPEN because its own note requires it to close in A01's PR. The refusal path is real and reaches the reader: answerQuestion resolves an unmatched question to NO_ROUTE with a stated refusal, the box renders that statement, and the store holds refused rows with their question text. G05 rule 4d did not weaken it - destinations refuse on no evidence, a tie between two destinations refuses, and a bare topic word never becomes a destination. ONE OBSERVATION recorded rather than claimed as a defect, because it is matching precision and not fabrication: 'what will the weather be like on election day' routes to elections-voting on the word 'election' and answers about who runs elections. Everything rendered was sourced and nothing was generated, so A07's contract holds; the answer is simply about a question nobody asked. Whether the matcher should require more than one hit before routing is a matching question for A01's build, and this is the note that hands it over. || 2026-08-17 (g12). CLOSED with A01. The contract is unchanged and now covers two more rungs. THE CLASSIFIER IS GOVERNED EXACTLY AS THE KEYWORDS ARE: it selects among curated destinations, generates nothing, and cannot invent a route by naming one (a topic id off the curated list resolves to the refusal - asserted). Where it is pulled, over its ceiling or unreachable, a weak match reaches the reader as the stated refusal with the four destinations offered; there is no low-confidence fallback anywhere in the path. The proving case the author named is now a PERMANENT test (tests/ask-matcher.test.ts) and a permanent production walk check: what will the weather be like on election day carries one hit and must never again be answered with who runs elections. Verified end to end with no classifier available: NO_ROUTE, askWasAnswered false, refusal rendered.

Title: Vendor and statute review per source
What this is: One written paragraph per vendor recording what its terms actually say. A record for choosing routes, deliberately not a gate that blocks retrieval.
Opened by: 2026-08-12 · Fix the four defects found testing the Phase 4 build
Closed by: 2026-08-12 · Read Pima County's meetings from the Legistar API, and wr…
Detail: One written paragraph per vendor recording what its terms say — reconnaissance informing route selection. A RECORD, NOT A GATE: it does not block an adapter.
Session record: Blocks D12 and D13. Created 2026-08-12 because D01 was scoped without any of it. Each finding must also answer the state-law question of whether a vendor's terms can restrict access to records the public body is required to publish - see B09. Record the finding on the source's own row, with the document reviewed and the date. DONE 2026-08-12: written up in docs/vendor-review.md, one section per vendor plus the statute question. Branch claude/legistar-adapter-and-vendor-review. Evidence: test (95 pass), lint and build all green. FINDINGS. Granicus/Legistar: terms revised 2026-07-20, California law, scoped to "this website", NO automated-access clause of any kind (checked for specifically); a documented public API exists and GET returns only what the client already marked public, so the terms are not even the operative question. CLEARED - build on the API, do not scrape *.legistar.com HTML. Hyland/OnBase (NEW vendor, found via Tucson): terms EXPLICITLY prohibit scraping and any robot/spider/data-mining, prohibit commercial exploitation, and prohibit use to build a competitive product; they enumerate five hyland.com hosts and do NOT list hylandcloud.com where tenants live, but that gap is thin evidence and Diligent proves a vendor states a product carve-out plainly when it means one. DO NOT BUILD - route to the Tucson Clerk and the City GovDelivery list instead, see D16. Diligent: carve-out confirmed VERBATIM - "If there is any conflict between these Terms of Use and Diligent standard terms for its products and services, Diligent standard terms will apply and take precedence" - so the website ToU is by its own instruction not the governing document for a tenant portal. NOT CLEARED and NOT BLOCKED; try the portal subscribe channel and the district own site first, escalate to B09. STATUTE. AZ A.R.S. 38-431.02 requires the agenda posted on the public body website 24h ahead - the strongest form of the B09 argument. AZ A.R.S. 39-121.03 cuts the other way and is the one for counsel: a records request for a COMMERCIAL PURPOSE requires a purpose statement, permits commercial-market pricing, and permits the custodian to ask the Governor to prohibit it outright; the definition reaches "any purpose in which the purchaser can reasonably anticipate the receipt of monetary gain from the direct or indirect use of the public record". Probably does not reach passive retrieval of an already-published page (it attaches to a request to a custodian, i.e. ladder rung 9) but the indirect-gain language is broad and this product sells aggregates - flagged for B09, not resolved here. NJ N.J.S.A. 10:4-8 requires 48h notice including the agenda only "to the extent known". NH RSA 91-A:2 requires notice but DOES NOT REQUIRE AN AGENDA AT ALL - see D17, this changes product wording. 2026-08-13 REDEFINED FROM GATE TO RECORD per the reprioritization and the public-records constraint now in CLAUDE.md: a vendor paragraph is reconnaissance informing route selection, never a veto over retrieving records a public body is statutorily obliged to publish. docs/vendor-review.md header updated to say so; paragraphs added for CivicPlus, Apptegy, Diligent Community/CivicWeb (MeetingsService), IQM2 and Revize, and the Hyland section rewritten with the D16 reversal keeping the original conclusion visible. Title: Decide the OCD-ID convention and reconcile to the canonical list

Closed by: 2026-08-13 · The cheap corrections: D15 marked, M14 built, GEOID retai…
Detail: The identifiers this repo builds do not match opencivicdata/ocd-division-ids. OCD-IDs are the only join key, so this blocks the body registry.
Session record: 2026-08-12. Was docs/state.md 5.2 item 8 ('verify before Phase 5'); checked and it fails, so it is now a blocker for Phase 4.6 rather than Phase 5. Evidence, against the full 194,977-identifier canonical list: state:az/school_district:* matches ZERO - the canonical form nests under county and suffixes the name, e.g. state:az/county:pima/school_district:tucson_unified_district vs this repo's state:az/school_district:tucson_unified. New Jersey places nest under county (state:nj/county:morris/place:rockaway) while New Hampshire's are flat (state:nh/place:newbury), so the nesting rule varies by state. The canonical list also appears to omit NJ townships entirely: county:morris/place:rockaway is present, Rockaway Township is not, even though it is a separate municipality with its own council. Separately, this work established that NAME alone is not a unique key even within one county - Morris County has both Rockaway borough and Rockaway township, and 30 NJ subdivisions collide that way - so county subdivisions are now nested under county and slugged from NAMELSAD; tests/subdivisions.test.ts pins that. THE DECISION: adopt the canonical shape wholesale (rebuilds every committed boundary file, and it is unclear the canonical list covers NJ townships at all), keep this repo's shape as an internal key plus a reconciliation table mapping to canonical with a confidence score per 4.7.2, or something between. Hard to reverse once officeholder and meeting rows carry the key, so it is the author's call. Phase 4.6's registry tables are designed and ready to build behind it. 2026-08-12 THE COST OF LEAVING THIS OPEN IS NO LONGER HYPOTHETICAL - 4.6.10 found the mismatch live and SILENT. The mock fixtures carried flat identifiers (state:nh/place:newbury, state:nj/place:rockaway_township, state:az/school_district:tucson_unified) while the registry nests NH/NJ subdivisions under county and suffixes the type (county:merrimack/place:newbury_town, school_district:tucson_unified_district). Five of eleven in-clip fixture divisions matched NOTHING. Tucson and the three counties happened to match, so the popup looked correct in Arizona and simply had no body link in Newbury or Rockaway, with no error logged anywhere - the silent zero-match join again, third occurrence. Fixed by correcting the fixtures to the registry's identifiers, which is right because the registry is Census-generated and the fixtures were hand-written before it existed. tests/link-ladder.test.ts now asserts the match count AND the denominator, and names the three deliberately-out-of-clip Cochise divisions explicitly so a clip can never read as a broken join nor a broken join hide behind 'probably the clip'. This does not decide D15 - it is evidence for how much a deferred identifier decision costs. 2026-08-13 DONE. The convention was settled and implemented on 2026-08-12 and the row simply never moved: this repo OCD-ID is the authoritative internal and interop key, and the canonical identifier rides alongside with a CanonicalMatch confidence (exact 528 / high 64 / none 348 as of the current registry build). The reasoning stands in docs/state.md 4.3: adopting the canonical shape wholesale is the one option that can LOSE a government (Rockaway Township is absent from the canonical list), while carrying both keeps every division and gains the mapping where it exists — the 4.7.4 national shape anyway. What remains is the 348 divisions with no canonical match, concentrated in county subdivisions — opened as D24 rather than holding this row open. M14 was blocked on this and is now unblocked and built. Branch claude/composite-source-and-reprioritization; test, lint, build green.

Title: The meetings snapshot counts two things and states one number
What this is: The meetings file counted two different things and reported one number, so a healthy-looking total hid a real discrepancy. Both numbers are now stated and have to reconcile.
Detail: The scheduled Refresh meetings snapshot job failed at least twice with snapshot holds 217 meetings but sources claim 193. The refresh was correct: 193 rows fetched fresh, 24 carried forward for schedulepage whose calendars the CI runner's egress cannot reach, 193+24=217. The invariant predated carry-forward and compared the total against the fresh count. The gate behaved correctly and nothing false shipped; the arithmetic was incomplete. Session record: 2026-08-17 (hotfix-0817, branch claude/h2-carry-forward-truth-0817). test 751 of 751 pass (13 new this session: 10 in tests/snapshot.test.ts, 3 in tests/refresh-corollary.test.ts), lint 0 errors 16 pre-existing warnings none in the touched files, build green (pnpm build, the command netlify.toml gives Netlify). DIAGNOSIS FIRST, and the brief's named suspect is CONFIRMED with one correction: carried rows were merged into the same meetings array as fresh ones with no field distinguishing them, so while the per-source carriedForward COUNT was recorded at write time it could not be RECOUNTED against the rows it counted - and no read path could tell a carried row from a fresh one. WHAT SHIPS: MeetingsSnapshot.counts is required and states fresh, carried, total; each carried Meeting carries carried: source plus lastFreshAt stamped at write time by carryForward (an existing mark is preserved, so a row carried through three failed runs still names the run that actually fetched it, instead of walking its timestamp forward one refusal at a time); reconcileCounts in lib/meetings/snapshot.ts enforces four equalities at the write boundary and on every read - fresh+carried=total, total=rows present, fresh=sum of per-source normalized (the ORIGINAL assertion preserved exactly and now aimed at the right number), and carried=the rows carrying the mark, per source as well as in total. NOTHING WAS LOOSENED: no >=, no tolerance, no skip-when-carried, and the forbidden repair of folding carried rows into normalized is itself a test that must still fail. PROVEN TO FAIL BEFORE TRUSTED: four mutations of the real committed file were each run against the real CI gate and each reddened - counts block removed, fresh disagreeing with the per-source sum, a carried row with no last-fresh instant, and fresh+carried not closing. END TO END: pnpm ingest composite run against the live portals, 10 of 10 sources reachable from this egress, 217 fresh + 0 carried = 217 written and validated; and because a developer's egress cannot reproduce the CI refusal, the 189+28 carry path was driven through the real carryForward and writeSnapshot on the real snapshot with schedulepage forced to fail - written, read back, marks intact, and the old invariant would have refused it with 217 !== 189.

Title: MapLibre vector tile fix
What this is: The map's rendering worker failed to load, so no map tiles were ever fetched. Without this fix there is no map.
Closed by: 2026-08-11 · Fix the MapLibre worker and port the EdiaStratMap design …
Detail: Turbopack raw-copies maplibre-gl-worker.mjs without rewriting its import of maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, so the worker 404s and no .pbf is ever fetched. Vendor both files into public/ so the relative import resolves, then delete the raster branch.
Session record: RESOLVED 2026-08-11 - see the RESOLUTION paragraph at the end; the diagnosis before it was partly wrong and is kept for the record. NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_RASTER=1 is a workaround that contradicts CLAUDE.md line 12 and must not ship. Re-vendor on every maplibre-gl upgrade. Also widen the error filter in map-canvas.tsx - it currently swallows anything not matching /style|sprite|glyphs|tile/i, including Failed to fetch. 2026-08-11 diagnosis only, fix NOT applied. Root cause confirmed in a production build, so it is not dev-only and the earlier React Strict Mode theory is retracted: the worker script itself serves 200, but its first statement imports ./maplibre-gl-shared.mjs, which 404s - Turbopack copies the worker into /_next/static/media/ byte-identical (verified by file hash) without rewriting the specifier, while emitting the sibling content-hashed as maplibre-gl-shared.<hash>.mjs. Module evaluation fails, the Worker error event carries an empty message that MapLibre never surfaces, and 0 .pbf requests are ever made while style.json, tiles.json and sprite all return 200. Evidence: resource timing on localhost:3000 production build, pbf=0. Also landed this session: CARTO silent fallback removed - buildRasterStyle returns null without a key and the caller shows the Basemap unavailable notice rather than substituting a provider; must-not-ship note added at the top of lib/map/style.ts citing CLAUDE.md line 12; basemap style pinned to basic-v2-dark. Two things to undo when the raster branch is deleted: (1) buildRasterStyle() now sets a glyphs endpoint, which exists only so the district label layer has fonts on the raster path - the vector style defines its own glyphs, so remove it with the branch rather than carrying it over. (2) firstSymbolLayerId in lib/map/districts.ts returns undefined in raster mode because that style has no symbol layers, so the beforeId insertion is inert and the district layers simply append on top; once vector rendering is restored, verify the ordering actually works and that basemap place names draw above the district boundaries. RESOLUTION 2026-08-11: two independent root causes, not one. (1) The worker. The Turbopack-specific part of the diagnosis above was too narrow - maplibre-gl 6 locates its worker at runtime via new URL(template, import.meta.url) built from a variable, which is not the static form any bundler rewrites, so webpack fails identically. Verified empirically: next dev --webpack still yields 0 .pbf and the same MIME-type error, so the webpack escape hatch was ruled out rather than assumed. Fix is scripts/build-map-worker.mjs, an esbuild step that bundles the worker and its shared sibling into one self-contained 461 KB public/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, wired to predev and prebuild so it regenerates on every maplibre-gl upgrade instead of drifting; the file is now gitignored and untracked, since a committed copy is exactly what goes stale. The script asserts the bundle has no unresolved imports left and fails the build if it does. (2) The district overlay had a second, unrelated cause that would have survived the worker fix. Attachment waited on map.once(idle), and idle requires style.loaded(), which requires every source to report loaded - but the MapTiler styles declare a maptiler_attribution source that is a vector source carrying only an attribution string, with no url, no tiles, and no layer referencing it. It has nothing to fetch, so its loaded flag is false forever, map.loaded() is never true, and idle never fires. Attachment now waits on getStyle().layers, the public signal that the stylesheet is parsed, which is the only precondition addSource and addLayer actually have. Evidence, measured in-page: 6 basemap tiles fetched from the .pbf template and all 6 parsed into buckets, 557 rendered basemap features across 13 layers including Water, so the land/water edge test passes; districts draw with 6 geojson-vt tiles, 11 rendered features, labels AZ-7 and AZ-6, ocdId ocd-division/country:us/state:az/cd:7. Note that .pbf fetches originate inside the worker and are invisible to main-thread resource timing, which is why the earlier pbf=0 evidence could not distinguish a dead worker from a throttled render loop; tile bucket state is the reliable signal. Raster branch, rasterBasemapEnabled, the NEXT_PUBLIC_MAP_RASTER flag and the OpenFreeMap fallback are all deleted; resolveBasemap now returns null without a key and the caller shows Basemap unavailable. The error filter in map-canvas.tsx now logs every MapLibre error and filters only which ones raise a user-facing notice. Branch claude/civic-map-entry-screen-4ey1cs; test (26 pass), lint and build all pass.

Title: NAMED REGRESSION: zooming out to z7 at 85701 wipes every pin

That is monotonic and correct at every rung, so lib/map/viewport-radius.ts and the ladder clamp are both behaving. THE DEFECT IS CLIENT-SIDE: the data is on the wire and the pins are not on screen. NOT DIAGNOSED, and deliberately not half-fixed under the deferral boundary: which client layer drops them. The probe counts entries whose element dataset.hidden is not 'true', so the two candidate shapes are (a) the pin pool marking every entry hidden at low zoom, or (b) the map effect's clip/mask - a known Chromium behaviour in this repo's own memory is that an OVERSIZED clip-path is dropped entirely, and projected geometry at z7 is far larger than at z11, so a mask that hides outside a region would hide everything the moment it is dropped or inverted. Reproduced 1 of 2 runs, both against production, minutes apart, same build. WHAT THAT RULES IN: a timing shape, not a geometry one - a deterministic clip-path or culling bound would fail every run. The pool sits at ZERO for 200-500ms (median 300ms) on EVERY zoom-out that re-queries, with inFlight 1 and the card beside it already showing data-refreshing true. Title: Identifier convention for governments Census does not enumerate
What this is: A naming convention for the thousands of governments no national standard enumerates — community college districts, special districts, authorities, joint boards — minted in the product's own namespace rather than faked in somebody else's.

Detail: The national-scale question D28/D29 surfaced and deliberately did not answer: community college districts, special districts, authorities and joint bodies exist as governments with no Census division, and this registry now carries them with ocdId null under a documented curated: id scheme (curated:az/pima-community-college#governing). Evidence from the wiring: (1) PCC is LIVE and serving meetings but is invisible to every geographic surface - coverageAt resolves by polygon containment, so a division-less body never appears in who-governs-here, and the jurisdiction dropdown skips it; (2) the venue cache key degrades to (sourceId, rawLocation) for null bodies and collides the day two division-less bodies share a source; (3) the meetings table's ocd_id is NOT NULL with a paired vintage - unwritable for these meetings when adapters start persisting; (4) the PHA case shows the boundary is blurry (a real authority whose board is the city council, wired under place:tucson). Options when taken up: follow opencivicdata's convention where one exists (check state:az for community_college_district entries), mint under a documented local convention reconciled via D24, or wait for the Census of Governments special-district pipeline (suspended 4.7). ~39,555 special districts nationally inherit this answer.
Session record: 2026-08-17 (g10). CONVENTION SETTLED ON EVIDENCE, and both named consequences fixed. Branch claude/g10-env-and-queue-0817; test 887 pass (8 new in tests/curated-divisions.test.ts), lint 0 errors, tsc clean, build green. STEP 1, WHAT OPENCIVICDATA ACTUALLY DOES, read 2026-08-17 from identifiers/country-us.csv (194,977 identifiers): THERE IS A CONVENTION AND IT IS CONSISTENT. A special district gets a segment named for its FUNCTION, nested under the county that contains it (or the state where it spans counties), slugged from its own published name — state:ca/county:los_angeles/water:castaic_lake_water_agency, state:nc/county:carteret/sanitation:harkers_island, state:mn/county:hennepin/park_district:1, state:il/sewer:mwrd. Six such segment types exist nationally — water, sanitation, sewer, park_district, health_care, transit — across FIFTY-ONE identifiers in the whole country. There is no community_college segment anywhere in the file; the phrase appears only twice, as school_district: slugs for two Maricopa DBAs. STEP 2, AND IT DECIDES THE ANSWER: the list carries NONE of the governments this repo needs. Arizona's segment types in full are country, state, cd, county, council_district, precinct, school_district, court_of_appeals, place, ward, sldl, sldu. Not one of the seven special districts D19 found inside Pima County's own agendas, and not Pima Community College. STEP 3, THE DECISION: ADOPT THE SHAPE, MINT IN OUR OWN NAMESPACE. lib/ocd/curated.ts holds it with the evidence above. The shape is followed exactly, so if these are ever contributed upstream or the upstream list grows to cover them the two agree by construction and the D24 reconciliation closes them the same way it closed the rest. The namespace is ours because writing an OCD path opencivicdata does not carry, in opencivicdata's namespace, is a minted identifier wearing a public vocabulary's clothes and indistinguishable downstream from a real one — the fabrication rule one layer more abstract. So curated:ocd-division/country:us/state:az/county:pima/water:ajo_domestic_water_improvement_district: strip the prefix and you have the identifier we would propose; keep it and nothing can mistake ours for theirs. IT MINTS NOTHING BY ITSELF, and that is deliberate — a curated id is created only where a government has been READ off its publisher's page, the standard every curated body row already meets. The seven districts stay UNRESOLVED with their agenda headings as evidence: a heading proves a government acted, it is not a source for its name or its boundary. CONSEQUENCE 1 FIXED (the venue key that collapses): bodyOcdId was null for a division-less body, and null === null, so the cache treated EVERY division-less body on a source as one body and would hand a reader the wrong building. Not hypothetical — Diligent serves three tenants and one, Pima Community College, has no division. venueScope() now substitutes a per-tenant value for a null, the three PCC rows carry tenant: 'pcc', and the diligent adapter passes its tenant; a test asserts a division-less row resolves for its own tenant and NOT for another. CONSEQUENCE 2 FIXED (the unwritable meetings row): meetings.ocd_id and division_vintage were NOT NULL, so the table could not hold a meeting of a government the Census does not enumerate — the first adapter to persist one would have failed, and the two repairs available were both worse than a nullable column (drop the meeting, which is D18 again, or mint a canonical id for a division that does not exist). Both are nullable now, WITH THE PAIRING ENFORCED BY THE DATABASE: migration 0007 adds CHECK meetings_division_vintage_pairing, (ocd_id is null) = (division_vintage is null), which is strictly stronger than the two NOT NULLs it replaces. Exercised against the local branch rather than assumed: both-set accepted, both-null accepted, each mismatch REFUSED by Postgres by name. Migration 0006 additionally makes location_name/lat/lng nullable and adds online_label/online_join_url, which D18 needs for the same reason. tests/db-schema.test.ts now asserts the pairing rather than the old spelling, and requires a CHECK wherever the pair is nullable — a rule only the application enforces is a rule the next writer skips.

THE WHOLE SPEC, so the next session starts from the brief and not from a summary: (1) a Yes on exactly ONE candidate in a contest RECORDS that candidate as the reader's pick — the pick section renders it chosen with the checkmark and a clear change/clear affordance, and does NOT ask again; (2) it ASKS only when the reader has said Yes to nobody, or Yes to more than one; (3) a recorded pick is never silently overwritten — if a reader with a pick (derived or explicit) then says Yes to a second candidate, the pick does not flip on its own: the section surfaces the CONFLICT and asks which one, and an EXPLICIT pick always outranks a derived one; (4) changing the pick does not alter per-candidate reactions and the two records stay separate; (5) the same rule for measures — a Yes/No on the measure IS the pick. WHY IT IS SAFE, recorded because it is the part that could go wrong: your-picks is device-local and never sold, so a DERIVED pick writes NOTHING into any aggregate and the sold per-candidate count remains explicit answers only. Title: handoff --ship leaves local main stale
What this is: The ship command merged the pull request and left the local repository a whole session behind, which made the project look empty on the next checkout.
Opened by: 2026-08-12 · Say what coverage means on screen, and stop counting 32 g…
Closed by: 2026-08-12 · Fast-forward local main after shipping, and push -u when …
Detail: --ship merges the PR on GitHub but never fast-forwards local main, so local main sits a whole session behind. Checking it out makes the repo look empty.
Session record: Found 2026-08-12 at session start. The working tree was on main at 64fee33 - the initial "Add files via upload" commit carrying only CLAUDE.md - while origin/main was at 2978324 with 26 commits and 118 files. Every phase of work was present and safe on origin; local main had simply never been updated, because scripts/handoff.mjs merges the PR through gh and then leaves the session on the feature branch. Nothing in the repo pulls main afterwards, so it goes stale by one session every time and the next checkout of main presents an apparently empty project. Recovered with git merge --ff-only origin/main: local main held zero unique commits and was a strict ancestor, and none of the untracked files (public/maplibre-gl-worker.mjs, screenshots/, next-env.d.ts, tsconfig.tsbuildinfo, .env.local) collided with a tracked path, so the fast-forward was lossless. 68/68 tests pass on the restored tree. Fix: have --ship fast-forward local main after a successful merge, and have the plain handoff check report main being behind origin/main as a warning - it currently only checks the branch against its own upstream and main against the branch, never local main against origin/main, which is the exact gap that hid this. SECOND GAP IN THE SAME SCRIPT, hit 2026-08-12: --ship refuses outright on a branch that has no upstream yet (ship() returns early on "refused - no upstream to push to"). It assumes the branch was already pushed by hand at some point, which is true for a long-lived branch and false for every new one - so the first --ship of every session fails until someone runs git push -u by hand. It should push -u origin HEAD itself when there is no upstream, which is the same one-line class of fix as fast-forwarding main afterwards. Both ends of the script assume a branch that already exists on the remote. FIXED 2026-08-12, branch claude/fix-r07-fast-forward-main. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green. All three parts of this row are closed. (1) --ship fast-forwards local main after a successful merge, via git fetch origin main:main - it moves the ref WITHOUT touching the working tree and refuses anything that is not a fast-forward, so a diverged main is reported, never flattened. Git rejects that fetch form when main is the checked-out branch, so from main it is git merge --ff-only origin/main instead. It runs after the post-ship re-measure and before git-state.txt is rewritten, so the report and the mirror file both describe the state the session actually ends in. (2) --ship pushes -u origin HEAD when the branch has no upstream instead of refusing; a branch created this session having no upstream is the normal case, and refusing meant the first ship of every session failed until someone ran git push -u by hand. (3) The plain handoff check now reports local main against origin/main as its own checklist line, which is the comparison nothing else made - branch vs its own upstream and main vs the branch both read clean while local main sat a session behind. SAFETY: fastForwardMain refuses when local main is AHEAD of origin/main and says so rather than doing anything, and git rejects the non-fast-forward underneath as a second line of defence. Verified both: with a commit only on local main the check reported "diverged - 0 behind, 1 ahead of origin/main" and a manual git fetch origin main:main was rejected non-fast-forward with the local ref unmoved. Verified in a sandbox with a bare local origin rather than reasoned about: a branch with no upstream got one from --ship ("feature pushed, now tracking origin/feature"); after advancing origin main to simulate the merge, the plain check warned "2 commit(s) behind origin/main - git fetch origin main:main"; that fetch fast-forwarded the ref with git status --porcelain empty afterwards, proving the working tree is untouched. The gh-dependent PR steps cannot run against a local remote, so the full --ship path was exercised for real when this row shipped. The suggested command adapts to where you are standing - git fetch origin main:main from a branch, git merge --ff-only origin/main from main - because the fetch form is rejected for the checked-out branch and printing a command that cannot work is worse than printing none.

Title: session:start, and a dev server that can be stopped
What this is: Three checks at the start of every session and a development server that can actually be stopped, so a stale checkout cannot pass for a working one.
Opened by: 2026-08-12 · Check the three things that lie quietly, and stop the dev…
Closed by: 2026-08-12 · Check the three things that lie quietly, and stop the dev…
Detail: Three start-of-session checks and a pid-tracked dev server, so a stale main, a clobbered CLAUDE.md or last session server cannot pass for a working one.
Session record: 2026-08-12, branch claude/session-start-and-dev-server. DONE: test (79 pass), lint and build all green. THREE PIECES, one shared property - the environment lies quietly if you do not look. A stale main looks like an empty repo, a clobbered CLAUDE.md looks like a repo with no constraints, a stale dev server looks like a working build. None announces itself; each presents as a plausible working state that is the wrong one. Recorded as a table in docs/state.md section 8. 1. scripts/session-start.mjs (pnpm session:start): fetch and compare local main to origin/main, printing the commit count and the git merge --ff-only command on a miss (R07); check CLAUDE.md is roughly 10 KB, failing under 1 KB or on the bare @AGENTS.md line with a restore-from-mirror command and NEVER a suggestion to reconstruct it; check port 3000 is free; then start the dev server through pnpm dev so predev runs. Exits non-zero on any failure. --check runs the three checks and starts nothing, which is the form a hook wants since the plain form ends in a server that never exits. A DIVERGED main (commits both sides) is reported separately and gets no --ff-only suggestion, because it would refuse. 2. Dev-server lifecycle. pnpm dev is now scripts/dev.mjs, which spawns next dev and writes its pid to .dev-server.pid (gitignored), removed on any exit it lives to see. predev is check-port.mjs then build-map-worker.mjs: it refuses when 3000 is in use rather than letting Next slide to 3001, naming the occupying pid, whether it is this repo own server, and the kill command. Sliding to 3001 is the failure worth preventing - scripts/shoot.mts targets a fixed localhost:3000, so screenshots would be of the old build AND the old map worker, since predev is where that bundle regenerates. 3. pnpm handoff stops the dev server before syncing the mirror, as its own checklist line. Non-fatal when nothing is running. It will NOT kill on a guess: something on 3000 with no matching pid file is reported foreign, with pid and kill command, for a person to decide. If the port is still held after the kill it FAILS and exits non-zero - a handoff reporting the session closed while something still serves is a false report. TWO THINGS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The pid holding the socket is NOT the pid in the file: Next runs the server in start-server.js, a grandchild of next dev. Measured - file recorded 5544, port held by 5816, and the stale server found at session start was four processes deep (17608 cmd shim -> 27420 next dev -> 23496 start-server -> 25956). So kills take the tree and the file-matches-occupant test is descent, not ===; an identity test would call this repo own server a stranger and withhold the kill that works. Second, dev.mjs resolves next/dist/bin/next and runs it under node rather than through the .cmd shim, because the old "dev": "next dev" put cmd.exe /d /s /c between pnpm and Next and killing a shim on Windows can orphan what it launched. FOUND A REAL ONE ON THE FIRST RUN: session:start --check failed on port 3000 held by pid 23496, a next dev started 16:06 that had survived the previous session handoff - exactly the gap this closes. It reported foreign rather than killing it, because it predated the pid file. All paths exercised rather than reasoned about: clean pass; the real stale server; predev refusal both directly and through pnpm (confirming the && chain works in a pnpm script on Windows and that Next never starts); pid file written on dev and removed when Next was killed underneath the wrapper; handoff --check reporting without killing; handoff killing the tree and confirming the port free; foreign holder warning; and the still-occupied path forced with a decoy pid plus an independent holder, which failed and exited 1. Does NOT close R07. session:start reports stale main and prints the fix; --ship still does not fast-forward, and the handoff checklist still does not warn. 2026-08-13, branch claude/deploy-snapshot-and-demo: the missing half added — session:start now KILLS a stale dev server it can attribute to this repo (pid file match) instead of failing, still fails on a foreign occupant, and after starting waits for / to serve then verifies the port holder descends from the child it spawned, printing the HEAD sha served. Verified live: killed-and-started clean, confirmation line printed.

Title: clerksboards parser reads past published month restrictions and exceptions
What this is: Three Tucson boards publish schedules with exceptions the parser ignored, so the product showed meetings those boards had not scheduled.
Detail: Three of Tucson's 27 wired Clerk boards publish a schedule the parser expands more broadly than the body wrote it. Board 40: '2nd Tuesday of each month September through May @ 6:00 p.m.' - the September-through-May restriction is ignored, so June, July and August sittings would be emitted. Boards 58 and 59: '1st Thursday of each month @ 9:00 a.m. (except January it will be 01/08/26 and July will be 07/09/26)' - the parenthetical exception is ignored, so those two months get the ordinary Nth-weekday date instead of the published one. Neither produces a wrong date inside today's serving window, because the recurrence loop only walks five months ahead from the window start; both will as soon as the window or the loop widens. This is one class, not three instances: the grammar has no representation for a restriction or an exception attached to a recurrence. Found 2026-08-18 (g19) by re-running the classification over all 56 board pages, and recorded rather than fixed under the addition rule.
Session record: Opened 2026-08-18 (g19 item 1b). The fix has a shape already: monthsInParens() in lib/sources/clerksboards/index.ts reads a month set out of a parenthetical for grammar C, and the same helper is what a restriction clause needs. The exception form is different - it is a date OVERRIDE for a named month, so the recurrence has to be expanded first and then patched, which is why it is not a one-line change. A test must assert the negative (no June/July/August date for board 40) as well as the positive, because the current window hides the defect and a test written against today's window would pass on a broken parser. || 2026-08-19 (g20). FIXED, and it took the session's item 1d with it - three of D29's 27 wired boards were emitting dates the body never published, so a wired claim over them was not finished. Recorded as a deliberate call under the addition rule: this was g19's row rather than a defect found here, and it sits inside the item this session owns. lib/sources/clerksboards/index.ts now reads both halves of the class the grammar had no representation for. (1) A SEASON RESTRICTION: monthRestriction() reads 2nd Tuesday of each month SEPTEMBER THROUGH MAY and expands to the nine months the body actually sits. The range WRAPS the year end, which matters - read as an ascending span it returns nothing at all. Board 40 now yields 9 dates across months 1-5 and 9-12, and June, July and August are gone. (2) A PER-MONTH DATE OVERRIDE: monthOverrides() reads (except January it will be 01/08/26 and July will be 07/09/26) out of an exception parenthetical and lets the published date beat the rule. Boards 58 and 59 now put January on 01/08 and July on 07/09 instead of the ordinary 1st Thursday, and every other month keeps the rule. An override is written for ONE year, so in a later year the month yields NOTHING rather than the rule's date - we know only that the ordinary rule did not hold and not what replaces it, the same reasoning as grammar D's TBD month. THE RULE THAT MAKES BOTH SAFE RATHER THAN MERELY BETTER: unreadableQualifier() DECLINES the whole board when the text carries the words of a restriction or an exception from which neither was extracted. A grammar that silently ignores a clause it does not understand is this defect exactly, and declining costs us a board while guessing costs a reader a wrong date under a government's name. Also fixed in passing: monthsInParens() now refuses an exception parenthetical, which also names months and means the opposite - reading one as a month set would cut a monthly board to two sittings a year. A SECOND DEFECT THE FIX SURFACED, and it was the opposite sign: the recurrence loop walked a FIXED five iterations, which only looked like the serving window. The cursor is normalised to the 1st of the window's opening month, so five months from May 1 reach September while the window itself runs to October 18 - every monthly board was silently losing its LAST IN-WINDOW SITTING on every run. Not an invented date; a real published one, dropped, and a count check would not have caught it because five months walked and about five meetings emitted. The loop is now bounded by the window (24-iteration runaway guard, the same one grammar C uses). 6 new tests in tests/clerksboards.test.ts, run against a FULL-YEAR window on purpose - this row's own note says a test written against today's window would pass on the broken parser, and it would have - asserting the NEGATIVE first (no June, July or August for board 40) as well as the positive. RE-DERIVED AFTER THE FIX against all 56 live Clerk pages: still 27 parseable, 0 boards lost. Branch claude/g20-deferred-queue-0819; pnpm test 1104 pass 0 fail, tsc --noEmit clean.

Title: walk:all reads a rendered outcome once after a fixed wait, in 33 more places
What this is: The production walk checked a rendered result once after a fixed wait, so a slow but working page reported as a regression. Fixed in 33 more places.
Detail: Three checks in scripts/walk-all.mts reported working surfaces as NAMED REGRESSIONS this session because they slept a fixed interval and then read the DOM once. A fixed wait plus a single read cannot tell GONE from NOT YET.
Session record: OPENED 2026-08-18 (g14) as the class behind three separate false reports in one session, all against the same build. (1) THE PIN FLOOR (R47): the zoom check slept 4000ms and read the pin count once, so a 200-500ms window at zero was caught on some runs and not others - reported as 'reproduced 1 of 2 runs, a race' when continuous sampling showed 4 of 4. (2) THE ASK REFUSAL (A07): slept 4500ms and read once; the classifier is a network round trip measured at 3190ms, 3171ms, 8397ms and 3166ms across the four zips, so whichever zip was slow that run failed. Walk 1 failed 85701 and 07866; a probe minutes later found those two fast and 85641 slow - proof it is a race and not per-zip behaviour. (3) THE A02 DIGEST: read the DOM with NO wait at all, at whatever moment the preceding geometry checks happened to finish. It passed the whole suite on one run and printed 'no digest rendered' at 85701 and 85641 on the next, twenty minutes later, about a digest that renders. ALL THREE ARE FIXED and each now waits for an OUTCOME rather than a duration - polling until the thing it is asking about has settled, then reading, with the read happening anyway at the ceiling so a genuine absence still fails on the truth. THE CLASS AUDIT, stated as a count rather than described: scripts/walk-all.mts contains 36 waitForTimeout calls. Three are converted. THE OTHER 33 ARE NOT AUDITED INDIVIDUALLY and that is stated rather than implied - most are legitimate settle waits after a navigation or a click rather than waits on a rendered outcome, and converting all of them blindly at the end of a session would be a large untested change to the one instrument every session depends on. WHAT THIS ROW IS: walk the remaining 33, decide for each whether it is waiting for a SETTLE (fine as it is) or for an OUTCOME (must poll), convert only the second kind, and state the split. THE TEST that a conversion is honest: it must never wait until the check PASSES. Waiting for an outcome means waiting until the surface has said something - a refusal or an answer, a count or a named gap - and then judging what it said. A poll that exits only on success would turn every one of these into a check that cannot fail, which is worse than the flake it replaces. WHY THIS IS A P2 AND NOT A P0: a false NAMED REGRESSION is loud, not silent - it costs a session's time and it erodes trust in the suite, but it never ships a wrong number to a reader. The direction of the error matters and it is the safe one. || RESOLVED FOR THE ASK FAMILY 2026-08-18 (g14), same session, and the class count is restated. THE ROOT CAUSE, after three wrong fixes each disproved by production rather than by argument: five questions were asked in a row on ONE page, and the previous answer is still on screen when the next is submitted. (a) Waiting until an outcome is PRESENT latched onto the previous outcome and read while the panel was being cleared - settled in 2089ms about a question a fresh-page probe measured refusing at 8161ms. (b) Waiting until the panel TEXT CHANGED and an outcome is present failed too, for a reason obvious once seen: the typed question is INSIDE the panel, so the text changes the instant the input is filled while the old answer is still rendered - settled in 262ms, and it turned A07 red at three zips, worse than the state it replaced. (c) Broadening the weak-match condition to accept a DESTINATION was added on evidence that later proved to be an artifact of the same staleness - 85641 printed destination=meetings for three walks, and once pages were fresh that destination stopped appearing at all. The clause stays, but on the check own documented intent (its comment names three honest outcomes and check 1 already treats destination as one), NOT on that reading, and the code comment now says so rather than leaving a wrong explanation behind. THE FIX THAT HELD: every ask question gets a FRESH PAGE. There is no reliable way to tell a stale outcome from a new one on a page that already has one, so the page stops already having one - which is this repo own standing note about the per-zip loop applied rather than worked around. Cost: one reload per question. RESULT: pnpm walk:all against production 534f631 is 302 ok, 0 FAIL, 0 named regressions, with the ask checks settling consistently at 3.1-5.3s where they had been reporting 262ms and 2089ms. WHAT REMAINS OPEN, and it is why this row stays Open rather than closing: the ask family is 4 of 36 waitForTimeout calls in scripts/walk-all.mts. THE OTHER 32 ARE STILL NOT AUDITED INDIVIDUALLY. The walk-and-split described above is unchanged for them - decide per call whether it waits for a SETTLE (fine as it is) or for an OUTCOME (must poll, and on a page with no stale outcome to find), and state the split. The test for an honest conversion is unchanged and was earned twice over here: it must never wait until the check PASSES.|| 2026-08-18 (g16, branch claude/g16-deploy-leaks-queue-0818). CONVERTED, WITH THE COUNT STATED AND GUARDED. OLD COUNT 36 (R49's own audit, 3 converted). NEW COUNT 12, every one of them justified in a comment directly above it, and a test refuses both directions. THE TWO BIGGEST ARE NOT VISIBLE IN THAT NUMBER: openAt and openWideAt each slept NINE SECONDS after every page load, roughly sixty page loads a run - about nine minutes of a walk spent waiting for a duration. THE THREE JUSTIFIED FORMS, each with its own marker so the test can tell them apart: R49 POLL INTERVAL (how often a poll asks; the loop exits on an outcome), R49 SAMPLING INTERVAL (the continuous sample that IS the R47 fix), and R49 DURATION, DELIBERATE (the wait is the assertion - outlasting a timer that must NOT fire, letting a compositor paint after a layer is hidden, or holding still for a geometry read that would be wrong mid-flight). tests/walk-waits.test.ts asserts every remaining call carries one of the three AND that the count may fall but never rise; PROVEN TO REFUSE by planting a bare waitForTimeout(1234) into openAt, which failed both assertions by name, with a green control after. Title: Key votes: resolve the LAWS half via the congress.gov API
What this is: The Senate publishes official long titles rather than the names people use, so searching for a vote by its popular name could never work. Resolved through the Congress API instead.
Detail: B15's named remainder. The Senate's roll-call lists publish official long titles, not popular names, so a popular-name search structurally cannot resolve the 20 law rows. The route: congress.gov API (CONGRESS_API_KEY already present) to search each law by title, take its bill number from the official record, then take that bill's roll calls in BOTH chambers - including which of two votes counts where a chamber voted twice (BSCA and OBBBA each name theirs in whichVote). House roll calls come from clerk.house.gov's own per-year XML.
Session record: Recorded 2026-08-15 with the finding that produced it, so the next session starts from the diagnosis rather than repeating it. The 20 explainers are already written and author-reviewable; only the roll-call resolution is open. || 2026-08-15 DONE (the truth session, branch claude/truth-session-0815). 0 of 20 law rows to 18 of 20, and the two that are not are STATED. THE ROUTE, every step of it the official record: (1) the public-law lists /v3/law/{congress}/pub for 116-119 — every entry but the pending one became law, so that is the bounded universe the bill must be in; (2) /v3/bill/.../titles, which is where the reader's name for a law actually lives ('Popular Titles | Inflation Reduction Act of 2022') — an entry resolves to the law whose titles carry its curated popular-name phrase and to nothing otherwise; (3) that bill's /actions recordedVotes, each carrying the chamber, session, roll number and the chamber's OWN url (clerk.house.gov / senate.gov), never one constructed here. No bill number is typed anywhere. THE APRIL 2024 SHAPE, resolved mechanically: the House voted on FOUR separate bills and the Senate voted the four as one vehicle, H.R. 815 — so the enacted law carries the Senate's single vote and NO House recorded vote at all. The four siblings get their House votes through the enacted law's own relatedbills list, matched on the same popular-name phrase; four DIFFERENT House roll calls and ONE shared Senate roll call, which is the render the brief asked for. THE CATCH THIS RUN MADE BEFORE IT SHIPPED, and the reason the selection rule is what it is: matching BSCA's whichVote 'final passage' on the literal words picked House roll 212 — 'On passage Passed 230-190' — which is the House passing its own unrelated Byrne-grant version of S.2938 in May. The vote on the gun law is roll 299 in June, 234-193, when the House agreed to the Senate's amendments. That would have put every House member against a vote on a different bill under the name of the law that made news. THE RULE, stated rather than guessed: passage-and-concurrence questions only (cloture, motions to proceed, motions to table and budget waivers are excluded by text), then the LAST of them by the chamber's own timestamp, because that is the vote on the text that became law; a tie the timestamps cannot break is a miss. The rejected alternative was refusing all eight two-vote entries, which would have left the group emptier than the record actually is while the answer sat in the chamber's own timeline. Also fixed: /\bconcur\b/ matched none of the Senate's own 'Senate CONCURRED in the House amendment' final actions, which is how BSCA and CHIPS first came back as 'no passage or concurrence question' on bills whose concurrence votes were right there. THE TWO MISSES, both correct refusals: funding-fight has no unambiguous popular name among a congress full of Continuing/Consolidated Appropriations laws, and stock-trading-ban has not become law and says so on the card. Guarded in tests/key-votes.test.ts: 18/20 exact (not 'at least'), the chamber's own url per chamber, passage-type questions only with procedural text refused, per-chamber roll-call distinctness (the D40 family, with the April siblings' shared Senate vote as the one legitimate collision), and the BSCA tally pinned at 234-193. New script pnpm law-votes:fetch, with a committed titles cache so a re-run costs a handful of calls. Evidence: test 604 pass (1 new) / lint clean (7 pre-existing warnings) / build exit 0. || 2026-08-18 (g19). Confirmed standing and NOT re-run: the committed snapshot carries this row's work - 18 of 20 law entries, both chambers, verified against the chambers' own records. A congress.gov resolver written this session (scripts/law-votes-resolver.mts, scripts/fetch-law-votes.mts) reproduces the route generically and adds two rungs B17 did not have - a sibling pass that reads a folded-in bill out of the VEHICLE's own related-bills record (the April 2024 package: three of the four siblings appear in no public-law list under any title, because only the vehicle became law), and a pending-measure pass through the House's roll-call index. It is NOT run against the committed snapshot, because on several entries it resolves to the vehicle and finds FEWER House votes than are already recorded - running it would trade verified data for worse. Kept as capability with a non-destructive merge (a run may add refs and may never remove one, and a refusal is counted and printed) and a docblock naming what went wrong. The one entry it would genuinely add, the pending measure's House vote, was applied surgically instead.

Title: The deploy gate - pnpm handoff --ship runs the build Netlify runs, and refuses on failure
What this is: The ship command now runs the exact build the deploy host runs and refuses to ship on failure. A green merge had once served the previous build for an hour.
Detail: Born from main@705f73b: merged green, Netlify failed type-check on a walk SCRIPT, production served the previous build for an hour.
Session record: 2026-08-16 (branch claude/deploy-gate-0816). THE FAILURE: Netlify's build for 705f73b failed on scripts/walk-0815g.mts(313,23) TS18048 - 'found.zba' is possibly 'undefined'. Site code compiled clean; a walk script stopped the truck. THE TYPE ERROR: an undiscriminated union ({error:number} | {total,zba,first}) narrowed with `"zba" in found`, which narrows nothing because TS widens such a union so BOTH members carry every key with one optional-undefined. Fixed with a real `ok` discriminant, no ! assertion; an unreachable service now THROWS a named error while a zero count stays a loud failed check - a check(...,false) there would have read as 'the Zoning Board is missing from production', a different and far more alarming claim. DIAGNOSIS BEFORE THE FIX, both suspects tested: stale .next skipping the type-check is WRONG (a warm-cache pnpm build on the same tree reproduces the failure exactly - compiled in 718ms, then 'Running TypeScript ...', then the identical TS18048); the build ran BEFORE the file existed is RIGHT and is the whole answer - the last pnpm build was in the pre-documents checks, the walk script was written after, and between writing it and shipping only pnpm walk:0815g ran. An ORDERING gap, not a cache bug, which is what decided the gate's home. THE GATE: buildGate() in scripts/handoff.mjs runs `pnpm run build` - the exact command netlify.toml gives Netlify - with tsconfig.tsbuildinfo cleared first, before the first push, and refuses the ship on failure with the TS diagnostic printed (Netlify's log needs the author's login, so a gate that only said 'build failed' would move the wall rather than remove it). NOT tsc --noEmit: tsconfig includes .next/types/**/*.ts, the route types Next GENERATES during a build, so a bare tsc checks whatever they said last time and a bad route-handler signature is exactly what it could miss. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE, recorded: a .githooks/pre-push hook - it would catch a push that bypasses handoff, but it is installed by `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` which is per-clone and which session:start only REPORTS on, so it can be silently absent in a fresh clone; and it would fire on every WIP push, which is how a minute-long check gets --no-verify'd away. NO SKIP FLAG, deliberately. PROVEN by injecting a deliberate TS error into the same walk script and running the gate's body against it: refused with 'scripts/walk-0815g.mts(352,5): error TS2532 · Failed to type check.'; tree restored, tsc exits 0. tests/handoff-gate.test.ts guards the WIRING (called before the first push, result acted on, same command as netlify.toml, tsbuildinfo cleared, no skip flag) - a source scan on purpose, since running a production build inside pnpm test would take the suite from 3s to 2min and would be testing Next. Evidence: test 606 pass (2 new) / lint clean (8 pre-existing warnings) / build exit 0; gate green in 9s on the shipping run; PR #44 merged, main 6a6dbbd, production serving it ~4 minutes later. || 2026-08-17 (g7) THE GATE GAINS ITS SECOND HALF - a deploy is now verified to have LANDED, not merely to have built. On the author's earlier ruling: an endpoint returning the commit SHA the deploy was built from, so a deploy with no visible output is verifiable. THE GAP THIS CLOSES, stated precisely because the two claims are easy to conflate: R22 proves the TREE BUILDS by running the same command Netlify runs, before shipping. It cannot prove that what Netlify then SERVED is this commit. The hour of production serving a previous build is exactly the distance between them. NEW: app/api/build/route.ts. Returns commit, commitShort, branch, context and deployId from Netlify's COMMIT_REF/BRANCH/CONTEXT/DEPLOY_ID. Read at MODULE SCOPE with the full process.env.X property access written out literally - Next only inlines a build-time env reference it can statically see, and a dynamic read (process.env[name]) would return undefined at runtime, which is the quiet way this endpoint would report nothing forever. Absent variables render "unknown" rather than a plausible SHA: absence is never dressed as a value, and an endpoint that invents its own answer is worse than no endpoint. Served no-store, because a cached build stamp is precisely the lie it exists to prevent. Nothing enumerates process.env - only named, non-secret build metadata - since that is how a token reaches a public JSON body. WIRED: handoff --ship now calls verifyDeployLanded() after the merge and fast-forward succeed (and only then, or the SHA polled for would be the wrong one). It polls /api/build for up to 5 minutes against origin/main's sha and declares itself with the C05 synthetic-run header. A TIMEOUT REPORTS AS COULD-NOT-RUN, NEVER AS A FAILURE - Netlify's build queue is not this script's to wait on, and an unreachable service is not a missing feature, the same distinction walk:all draws. What it will not do is report success without having seen the SHA. IT ALSO CARRIES EVIDENCE FOR THE WRITE GUARD'S SECOND REMAINDER (R34): the response's buildEnv block reports what the BUILD saw and the runtime block reports what the SERVING PROCESS sees - NETLIFY, CONTEXT, DEPLOY_ID presence, NODE_ENV, and the dbRole the guard would conclude. A variable present in buildEnv and absent in runtime is a build-only variable the write guard must not depend on. That is a fact nobody could check without deploying and looking, which is why the guard was built on NODE_ENV and the tightening was deferred rather than guessed. VERIFIED LOCALLY against a real dev server: the route answers {"commit":"unknown", ..., "runtime":{"nodeEnv":"development","hasNetlify":false,"dbRole":"production"}} - honest on all counts, since a local build has no COMMIT_REF and WTP_DB_ROLE is unset. The Netlify-side values are readable on the first --ship after this lands. Branch claude/g7-dispositions-0817; test 793 pass 0 fail, tsc --noEmit clean, build green. || CORRECTED 2026-08-17 (g8), branch claude/g8-deploy-and-g7-queue-0817. THE BUILD-STAMP ENDPOINT SHIPPED WITH A FALSE PREMISE AND COULD NEVER HAVE VERIFIED A DEPLOY. Found by using it: after PR #72 merged, handoff polled /api/build for five minutes and production kept answering {""commit"":""unknown"",""buildEnv"":{""hasCommitRef"":false,...}} with HTTP 200. THE PREMISE, quoted from the row above: 'Next inlines a build-time env reference it can statically see' into the server bundle. IT DOES NOT. Next inlines for the CLIENT; server code keeps process.env.X as a RUNTIME read. Measured rather than reasoned about - the built chunk .next/server/chunks/_1nq4lm3._.js still contained the literal text 'process.env.COMMIT_REF??null'. Netlify sets COMMIT_REF in the BUILD environment and not in the function runtime, so the module-scope read ran at cold start, found undefined, and the endpoint reported 'unknown' on every request of every deploy. The failure the row's own header warned about, arriving through the other door: not a dynamic lookup defeating the inlining, but no inlining ever happening. THE FIX: next.config.ts's env key, which is the mechanism that actually substitutes at build time, exposing WTP_BUILD_COMMIT / _BRANCH / _CONTEXT / _DEPLOY_ID / _ON_NETLIFY; the route reads those. Build metadata only - anything inlined there is readable by anyone who can read the bundle. An absent variable is written as an empty string by the config and read as NULL by the route, because '' sliced to seven characters is a blank SHA rendered as a value, which is the render-default rule in the one place whose job is being trustworthy about which commit is serving. PROVEN EMPIRICALLY, twice over: COMMIT_REF=deadbeefcafe1234 pnpm build puts the literal into the server chunk AND removes process.env.WTP_BUILD_COMMIT from it (so it was substituted, not merely present), and next start then answers {""commit"":""deadbeefcafe1234"",""commitShort"":""deadbee""}. GUARDED: tests/build-stamp.test.ts, 5 tests, asserting the two files agree name-for-name - the rot this cannot afford is a name added to one and not the other, which reads as an absent variable and renders the same wrong 'unknown' while looking correct. The runtime block's direct reads of NETLIFY, CONTEXT and DEPLOY_ID are deliberately EXEMPT and separately asserted to still exist: they are the measurement R34's second remainder needs, not the defect. AND THAT MEASUREMENT NOW HAS AN ANSWER, which is a finding in its own right: on the live Netlify deploy the serving function sees NEITHER NETLIFY nor CONTEXT nor DEPLOY_ID (hasNetlify false, hasContext false, hasDeployId false, contextValue null) while the response headers say Server: Netlify with an X-Nf-Request-Id. So there is NO runtime signal from Netlify for the write guard to tighten on, and the guard must keep resting on NODE_ENV plus the belt. Recorded so the next session does not go looking for one.

Title: sendBeacon bypasses the synthetic-run header, so our own automated runs land ORGANIC
What this is: The browser's fire-and-forget send bypasses the header that declares an automated run, so the product's own robots were landing in the sold store labelled as readers.
Detail: lib/db/run-marker.ts declares a run through an HTTP header, and Playwright extraHTTPHeaders do not apply to navigator.sendBeacon. lib/log/client.ts PREFERS sendBeacon. Any event leaving by that path is recorded ORGANIC - our own robots counted as readers in the store we sell.
Session record: OPENED 2026-08-18 (g14), and it is opened because it BIT, not as a theory. THREE QUESTION_ASKED rows landed ORGANIC with run_id null at 2026-08-18T18:13:00Z, 18:14:12Z and 18:15:25Z, inside walk 7's window of 18:05:43Z to 18:16:18Z. They are ours. The exact window is recorded in docs/synthetic-runs.md so a correction is a filter and never a hunt. WHY IT SURFACED NOW rather than earlier: g14's fix for the ask checks reloads the page between questions, and a page unload is exactly when a queued beacon flushes. The hole was always there; the reload made it fire. That is worth stating because it means the row is about a LATENT hole in every browser script, not about the reload. FIXED FORWARD in 10 contexts - all 5 in scripts/walk-all.mts and 1 each in this session's five probe scripts (probe-r47, probe-m139, probe-a07, measure-load, shoot-ballot-pill) - by deleting navigator.sendBeacon in an addInitScript before the page loads, which forces the fetch fallback, and fetch DOES carry extraHTTPHeaders. THE COST IS STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: those runs no longer exercise the beacon transport at all. That is the right trade for now - a suite that pollutes the sold store on every run is worse than one that tests a transport one layer down - but it is a trade and a later session may prefer the other fix below. THE CLASS AUDIT, as a count: scripts/ holds 50 browser contexts. 10 are guarded. 40 ARE NOT, across 36 scripts - every tester-walk, every shoot, every measure, pairs, perf, overlap-audit, verify-sources-tab, walk-0815g, walk-r39, walk-r40 and walk-r41. Any of them run against production leaks the same way. WHAT THIS ROW IS: guard the remaining 40, and decide whether the guard is the right shape at all. THE ALTERNATIVE WORTH PRICING AT THE SAME TIME, because deleting a DOM method in every test is a workaround rather than a fix: teach the marker to travel in the BODY as well as the header. lib/log/client.ts already posts a JSON payload, so a run id read from a page-level global (planted by addInitScript) would ride inside it and survive both transports, and the route would trust the body only when the header is absent. That fixes the class once instead of once per script, and it would also cover any future transport. THE THREE ROWS ARE NOT BACKMARKED, deliberately: pnpm searchlog:backmark needs a write to production, and the only sanctioned write path is intake-limiter-purge (R43). Correcting them needs the author at the console or a new named sanction, and a session must not grant itself one. AUTHOR DECISION NEEDED on that correction; everything else here is ordinary work. || CORRECTED 2026-08-18 (g14), same session, and the correction is the point. THE FIRST FIX WAS A NO-OP: delete navigator.sendBeacon removes an OWN property, and sendBeacon lives on Navigator.prototype, so the method still resolved. It type-checked, it read correctly, and it changed nothing. Caught the only way it could be - by re-running the walk and checking a number that should not have moved. ORGANIC WENT 3 TO 7: four more of our own rows landed as readers in the very run meant to prove the fix. THE WORKING FORM, now in all ten contexts, is an explicit override: Object.defineProperty(navigator, "sendBeacon", { value: undefined, configurable: true }). VERIFIED BY MEASUREMENT rather than by reading it again - organic before a run that asks three questions: 7; organic after: 7; synthetic across the same run 2143 to 2150, so the events landed declared. THE FULL LEAK IS SEVEN ROWS, all QUESTION_ASKED, all run_id null, in two windows: 18:13:00Z, 18:14:12Z, 18:15:25Z (walk 7) and 18:34:23Z, 18:35:32Z, 18:36:43Z, 18:37:52Z (walk 8). Still not backmarked, for the reason already stated - it needs a production write nobody has sanctioned.|| 2026-08-18 (g16, branch claude/g16-deploy-leaks-queue-0818). CLOSED AS A CLASS, NOT AS A CENSUS. THE CONSTRUCTION OF A BROWSER IS NOW ONE FUNCTION: scripts/browser.mts exports launchGuarded, and 45 scripts - every script in the tree that drives a browser - come through it. It applies three things at construction, so none of them can be forgotten: the run header on every context; the sendBeacon override, installed by addInitScript before the page's first script runs; and a run id MINTED FROM THE SCRIPT'S LABEL when the environment set none. That third one is new and it closes a hole nobody had named: syntheticRunHeaders() returns an empty object for an unset WTP_RUN_ID, and an empty object means ORGANIC, so a forgotten export was a silent total leak. launchGuarded refuses to open a browser at all if the marker comes out empty. THE GUARDED API IS DELIBERATELY NOT NAMED LIKE PLAYWRIGHT'S: browser.context() and browser.page(), never newContext/newPage, because the whole guard rests on a test being able to refuse the raw names outright and it cannot do that if the guarded API answers to the same words. tests/browser-construction.test.ts asserts scripts/browser.mts is the only file that calls chromium.launch, browser.newContext or browser.newPage, and PROVEN TO REFUSE by planting browser.newContext( back into scripts/pairs.mts and watching it name that file, with a green control after. 7 duplicated local guard blocks were removed at the same time (walk-all.mts alone carried the same override FIVE times, twice per context in two of them) - the duplication was the census this row exists to stop. tests/run-marker-coverage.test.ts IS DELETED, and the deletion is the point: it asserted that a script MENTIONS syntheticRunHeaders in its source, which every leaking script did, so it was green through both leaks. What it covered that nothing covers now is recorded in the replacement's header - its 23-script exemption list is moot because those scripts are guarded by construction, and its covered>=8 floor is replaced by a far higher one. THE REPLACEMENT PROVES NON-LEAK BY BEHAVIOUR: tests/beacon-guard.test.ts opens a real browser through the shared site against a local capture server, makes the page fire the exact transport lib/log/client.ts prefers, and asks markerFromRequest - the production function that decides a row's class - what the landed request would be recorded as. SYNTHETIC, with the run id. It lands against a local server rather than production deliberately: proving this against the real store would add the pollution the guard exists to prevent, with no sanctioned write path to remove it (R43). The chain asserted is transport, headers on the wire, markerFromRequest, run class - everything but the INSERT. THE PLANT IS IN THE SUITE PERMANENTLY, not just run once: a second test builds a context the way the forty unguarded scripts built one and asserts it LEAKS, so a day when Playwright starts carrying the header itself fails loudly rather than leaving a guard that proves nothing. A NEW FINDING FROM WRITING THAT PLANT, and it sharpens this row's own diagnosis: THE HEADER IS NOT UNCONDITIONALLY LOST ON A BEACON. Measured four conditions - a beacon fired while the page is ALIVE arrives DECLARED; a beacon flushed at pagehide during a RELOAD arrives UNDECLARED; the same at a NAVIGATION arrives UNDECLARED; at page CLOSE it arrives declared. Title: The active-state model, built as specified - and the mask stops muting the state the reader is standing in
What this is: One state active at a time, the whole of it crisp at every zoom, every other state muted and lowered — and the mask stops dimming the state the reader is standing in.

Closed by: 2026-08-16 · The mandate becomes law before the hunting starts, and th…
Detail: The author's g5 item 1. One state active at a time; the WHOLE of it crisp at every zoom; every other state muted and lowered; no state active means no treatment at all. Zip shading removed from the product.
Session record: 2026-08-16 (g5), branch claude/active-state-model-0816. DIAGNOSED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY READING: at the zoom a reader lands on from a zip (z11) the ENTIRE frame was muted and blurred - no crisp pixel anywhere - while the reader stood in the middle of the active state. The mute is a DOM scrim carrying backdrop-filter, clipped to everything-except-the-active-state by clip-path: url(#...). The path fed to that clip was the state's rings projected at FULL EXTENT: measured on production, Arizona at z11 spans x -10869.4..5939.9 and y -16547.3..3432.1, about 16,800 x 20,000 CSS px. CHROMIUM SILENTLY DROPS A CLIP PATH THAT LARGE, and a dropped clip is not a smaller clip - the scrim then paints over its whole box. Proved by holding the TOPOLOGY fixed (viewport rectangle minus one enclosing rectangle, even-odd, an empty region at every size) and varying only the magnitude: +/-2000px gave chroma 17.39 detail 20.15, pixel-identical to the effect-disabled frame; +/-8000px and +/-20000px both gave chroma 11.24 detail 9.57, pixel-identical to the broken frame. Also found: the CSS `mask` on the scrim was INERT the whole time - Chromium does not resolve an SVG <mask> reference from CSS on an HTML element - so the clip was the only thing doing the work and its failure took the entire effect with it. Same class as g4's clamped SVG filter region: Chromium's answer to geometry it cannot rasterize is to drop it, and a dropped mask reads as FULL coverage, the loudest way an ambient effect can fail. FIX: lib/map/state-focus.ts#clipRingToBox - Sutherland-Hodgman per ring against the mask's own region (canvas + FILTER_PAD), applied after projection and BEFORE simplification. Nothing outside that box was ever visible, so the cut removes only geometry that was being rasterized to be thrown away, and it is also the cheapest frame win available. The case that looks identical in the code and opposite on screen is handled explicitly: a ring clipped to NOTHING means the viewport does not touch the active state, so the whole frame is muted (pan into New Mexico with Arizona active) - it used to clear the drawing and render plain, which is the no-active-state treatment. Holes survive the clip, so a viewport inside a hole cancels to nothing under even-odd, which is the truth. ZIP SHADING REMOVED WHOLE per the author's ruling: the tint, both layers, the source, the /api/zcta/<zip> route, lib/geo/zcta-outline.ts and the client fetch are deleted - not flagged off. Committed ZCTA geometry stays in the repo, unused. Its walk check is RETIRED with the feature and replaced by its opposite ('the zip draws nothing on the map'). NEW PERMANENT MEASUREMENT pnpm measure:focus (scripts/measure-focus.mts): the existing pnpm measure:extrusion passed at full marks on this broken build because it measures how SMOOTHLY the edge falls off, not WHAT is covered. The new one is anchored to lng/lat - real places projected through the live map - and asserts interior crispness far from the entered zip (north Tucson, Drexel Heights, the corners of the state), effect-off equivalence with the border excluded by the SHIPPED spec's own reach rather than by a constant, exterior muting compared point-against-itself, per-state data scoping off the network log, and no-active-state at 06716 and with no zip. Title: Stop losing search_log inserts, and be able to see it when one is lost
What this is: About one search in ninety was never recorded in the store this business sells, and nothing could see it happening. Diagnosed and fixed this session.
Detail: THE ALARM'S FIRST REAL FINDING, on its first day (Prompt D item 6). Two separate walk:all runs against production each raised exactly one write_alarm row for search_log: 2026-08-21T00:21:13Z and 2026-08-21T00:28:19Z [expected-future: real UTC instants read from write_alarm while the Phoenix day was 2026-08-20]. The first run landed 93 rows under its browser run id plus 9 under its fetch run id, so the failure rate is on the order of ONE IN NINETY-FOUR, not a one-off. WHAT IS KNOWN: error_code is NULL on both, so the driver supplied no SQLSTATE - a genuine Postgres refusal (a missing column, a constraint, a check) always carries one, and its absence points at a TRANSPORT failure between the Netlify function and the Neon HTTP endpoint rather than at the database rejecting anything. Production schema is IN SYNC at 16 of 16, confirmed by corepack pnpm db:check --target=production, so this is not D73 recurring. The message the alarm now stores is the query shape with its params stripped, which tells us which table and tells us nothing about why. WHY IT MATTERS: search_log is a SOLD store. A one-percent loss is invisible to every reader and shows up in a buyer's aggregate as a number slightly smaller than the truth, with no way to know it. Nobody could have known this before the alarm existed. THE SPEC: capture more about the failure before designing a retry - the alarm should store the error's constructor name and any driver-specific fields alongside the message, because 'no SQLSTATE' is a deduction and the row should carry the evidence for it. Then decide whether a bounded retry belongs on the write path or whether the Neon HTTP driver has a documented transient class with its own guidance. A retry written before the cause is named would be a guess wearing a fix's clothes.
Session record: 2026-08-20 (Prompt D item 6, found by the close-out walk). NOT P0 under the redefined bar - no reader-visible outcome is blocked - and that is exactly what makes it dangerous: the loss is invisible from every surface, which is the whole D73 family. The standing walk check no sold-store write raised an alarm in the last 24h is RED on this and is correct to be; it is a true positive and the first one the instrument produced. || 2026-08-20 (Prompt E item 4). TWO DEFECTS, BOTH OURS, BOTH ON THE WRITE PATH ONLY - the reader-facing catch is unchanged per RULING 25. (1) THE LOSS: app/api/meetings/route.ts called logSearchEvent() and never awaited it and never handed it to after(), and returned its JSON immediately below. On a serverless runtime the invocation ends when the response is returned and a promise still in flight is dropped - silently, with no rejection, so no .catch could ever see it. Prompt D fixed exactly this shape for the ALARM and left the INSERT five lines above it, which is the named-instance rule: one sighting of a floating promise on a sold-store write path was one of two, in the same function. (2) THE INSTRUMENT: lib/db/write-alarm.ts read .code and .message off the object it was handed. Drizzle hands it a DrizzleQueryError, whose own source (drizzle-orm/errors.js, read rather than assumed) is four assignments carrying no code and a message of 'Failed query: <sql>'. RULED OUT WITH EVIDENCE: a constraint violation (search_log carries only NOT NULLs and a gen_random_uuid PK - no unique, check or FK is reachable); a retry path reporting success (there is none, in either call site). RULED IN: the dropped promise, structurally. Title: The meetings refresh fails the whole run when one source finds nothing, and that does not scale
What this is: The refresh commits only if every source succeeded. One source producing zero rows from a non-zero fetch fails the run, so the snapshot does not move - even when carry-forward already saved that source's rows and every other source was fine. Today that is 14 failures of 37 runs. At national volume it means the snapshot never commits again, and the decision to make the gate per-source rather than per-run is yours.
Detail: The arithmetic, stated. 11 child sources at a 37.8% whole-run failure rate implies a per-source failure probability of about 4.2% per run. A national corpus needs a source instance per distinct feed or portal; at 5,000 of them the chance every one succeeds in a single run is (1-0.042)^5000, which rounds to zero. Even at a tenth of that per-source rate, 0.5%, it is 1.4e-11. The gate as written stops being a gate and becomes a permanent refusal to publish. What it protects is real and must survive: a zero-row extraction is a failed extraction and may never be written into the data as an absence. The proposal is that the run carries that source forward, commits everything else, and reports the failed source by name in its own summary - which is what the composite already computes and the workflow then throws away.

Title: pnpm doctor is not built
